item: The test and Core-only jobs run in three cost-balanced shards (C10, decision 27)
summary: Each of the two full-suite CI jobs (79:36 in one process on the parity run) is a matrix of three legs that run a third of the test files, chosen by scripts/ci_shard.py from a measured cost table (longest first to the least-loaded shard; a file the table does not name goes to crc32(path) mod 3). A leg ignores the other shards' files (--ignore lines in an argument file) instead of naming its own, because a path named on the pytest command line escapes collect_ignore. The required checks keep their names through two aggregators (test-all, core-only-all; if always(), green only if every leg succeeded). Measured on the proving run: Test legs 28:12 / 25:34 / 26:59, Core-only 17:46 / 28:22 / 25:54, required check green 29:51 after the run was created (goal about 25 min: not reached with three shards). Parity against one unsharded process on the same commit: 1580 modules, 29315 passed, 353 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 differences in any leg; the real core install collects 29440 tests in 1555 modules in both forms. One order dependence found and fixed at the leaker (test_scheduler_pause_resume.py left an oo-scrape-now thread).
